findings.fix_hint: revert to text interpolation (`{{ notif.text }}`) unless rich formatting is a genuine requirement; if HTML must be supported, keep interpolation for all error/status-derived text sources and only use [innerHTML] (with an explicit narrow allowlist, not plain strings) for notification text that is verified to never include backend/remote-derived content.
findings.problem: The hunk changes `{{ notif.text }}` (Angular text interpolation, which unconditionally HTML-escapes its content — no markup can ever execute) to `[innerHTML]="notif.text"`, which parses the string as HTML and relies solely on Angular's built-in DomSanitizer (a library default, not an unconditional guarantee) to strip dangerous constructs before render. I traced where `notif.text` originates: in src/angular/src/app/pages/main/header.component.ts:49 it is set to `status.server.errorMessage`, and at line 96 to `Localization.Notification.STATUS_REMOTE_SERVER_ERROR(status.controller.latestRemoteScanError)` (src/angular/src/app/common/localization.ts:15-16 does plain string concatenation, no escaping). `latestRemoteScanError` is deserialized verbatim from the backend's `latest_remote_scan_error` JSON field (src/python/web/serialize/serialize_status.py:37), which is set from `remote_scan.error_message` (src/python/controller/controller.py:633), itself `str(e)` of an exception raised during the remote seedbox directory scan (src/python/controller/scan/scanner_process.py:94). Since this app scans a user's remote seedbox (commonly used for torrent content, i.e. third-party-named files) for files to sync, scan-failure exception text can plausibly embed attacker-influenced strings (e.g. unusual remote file/directory names triggering a parse error), with zero HTML-escaping applied anywhere along this chain. This content now flows straight into `[innerHTML]`. Whether this specific payload achieves full script execution depends entirely on Angular's DomSanitizer continuing to strip every dangerous construct (a library-default guarantee that can regress or be bypassed, e.g. via a future bypassSecurityTrustHtml call elsewhere, or a sanitizer gap/mXSS edge case) — this is a demonstrated loss of the prior unconditional escaping guarantee, not merely a theoretical concern. Independent of sanitizer coverage, it already permits arbitrary benign-looking markup injection (hidden elements, fake buttons/links, layout/phishing content) into a notification surface shown to the user.
findings.title: Interpolation replaced with [innerHTML] binding enables HTML/script injection via remote-influenced notification text
findings.why_it_matters: Angular's text interpolation made script/markup injection structurally impossible for this field; this change makes safety conditional on the sanitizer always working, for content that traces back to backend/remote-scan error strings which can embed third-party-influenced text (e.g. remote file names). A single sanitizer gap, a future refactor that marks the value as trusted (bypassSecurityTrustHtml), or a different text source added later without the same care would turn this into a stored XSS executing in every user who views the notification bell.

agent_notes: Blast radius: the bell component sits in the app shell (app.component.html/ts), so every page and every one of the 9 Notification producers is affected: header.component.ts:47,74,104; settings-page.component.ts:95,167,236,254; file-list.component.ts:578 (via _showNotification at 523,531,552,558,564); version-check.service.ts:75.

Producers whose input comes from outside: server errorMessage, remote scan errors (output from the remote seedbox), bulk-action errorMessage, settings validation errorMessage. The Localization constants are static and safe. The version-check URL is already pinned to the ^https://github.com/ pattern (version-check.service.ts:61), but its NEW_VERSION_AVAILABLE string has no anchor markup, so even that producer gets nothing out of innerHTML.

No producer emits HTML today, so the change adds no working feature. It only adds an attack surface and a rendering regression. Its probable purpose (a clickable version link, per the Phase 68 'clickable version' commit) is better handled with a structured link field.
Elsewhere the repo escapes before innerHTML (confirm-modal.service.ts:33 escapeHtml before :100). This diff skips that convention.
No API, schema, or performance impact; the change is confined to the template.
Verdict: blocking issue. Revert the [innerHTML] binding (impact-001).

findings.fix_hint: Revert to `{{ notif.text }}`. If one producer (e.g. the version URL) really needs a link, add a typed structured field such as `linkUrl` instead of treating all text as HTML
findings.problem: The old `{{ notif.text }}` escaped all markup in every case. The new `[innerHTML]` parses the text as HTML, and the only thing standing between it and the DOM is Angular's default DomSanitizer. Several producers pass strings the backend or remote side controls straight into `text`: `status.server.errorMessage` (header.component.ts:49), `latestRemoteScanError` through STATUS_REMOTE_SERVER_ERROR (header.component.ts:96, localization.ts:15-16), the bulk `result.errorMessage` through Bulk.ERROR (file-list.component.ts:554, localization.ts:74-75), and settings `reaction.errorMessage` (settings-page.component.ts:170,239,257). Any of these can echo file names, remote shell output or config values. The sanitizer removes script tags and on* handlers but keeps `<a href>` and `<img src>`. So a remote file name or scan error like `<a href="https://evil.example">Click to re-authenticate</a>` or `<img src="https://tracker.example/x">` now renders as a working phishing link or a beacon that fetches from outside, inside a trusted DANGER notification.
findings.title: Notification text switched from escaped interpolation to [innerHTML], allowing HTML injection from server and remote error strings
findings.why_it_matters: A protection that held for every input has been swapped for one that depends on a library default sanitizer, and it now covers every notification producer, including ones that relay remote, attacker-influenced strings. It also breaks the user's absolute CLAUDE.md rule against rendering user-supplied content through innerHTML.

findings.fix_hint: Keep text interpolation; the producers emit plain text
findings.problem: Every producer builds plain text, not HTML (localization.ts template literals; raw server error strings). With innerHTML, a remote scan error such as `bash: <stdin>: line 1: syntax error`, a file name like `Tom & Jerry <1080p>.mkv` in a bulk error, or a config validation message like `expected <host:port>` gets parsed as markup. Tag-like pieces vanish and entities get decoded, so users see an incomplete or misleading error.
